note: Corrections applied after the round-0 adversarial fact-check. All 21 cards were verdict CONFIRMED on the underlying fact; these seven had wording that overstated or misrepresented the cited source. The critic never edits — these are applied here, in the pipeline, and re-verified.

epc-domestic-2030.body: One compliance date confirmed: 1 October 2030 for the new standard. The statutory instrument is still to come.
epc-domestic-2030.why: The original read as settled law. The regulations are expected in 2027; the date is a confirmed policy intention, not yet in force.

epc-cost-cap-10k.body: The retrofit cost cap rises from £3,500 to £10,000 per property. Budget for it, or register a ten-year exemption.
epc-cost-cap-10k.why: 'Trebles' was imprecise — £3,500 to £10,000 is 2.9x. Both figures now stated.

epc-nondom-current.body: Your commercial unit needs only EPC E today, unless a registered exemption applies. Tougher targets remain consultation.
epc-nondom-current.why: 'Every tenancy, no exceptions' was contradicted by the cited source: registered exemptions exist and short and very long leases fall outside MEES.

renters-periodic-tenancies.body: Fixed terms vanish. Nearly every tenancy converts to an assured periodic tenancy, ending on the tenant's notice.
renters-periodic-tenancies.why: 'Tenants stay as long as they like' overstated the reform — landlords retain every section 8 ground, including sale and moving in.

sdlt-standard-rates.body: Stamp duty bites from £125,000, and a 5% surcharge stacks on any additional home. Portfolio building just got pricier.

extraSource.name: GOV.UK — Rates of Stamp Duty Land Tax for non-UK residents (HMRC)

sdlt-standard-rates.why: Body unchanged and correct; a second source added because the non-UK-resident surcharge is not on the originally cited page.

london-house-prices.why: The quotation was not verbatim, so it is relabelled as a paraphrase rather than shipped inside quotation marks.

london-private-rents.body: London rents reach £2,302 but annual growth cools to 2.2%, the slowest in England. Leveraged landlords feel the squeeze.
london-private-rents.why: The 11.5% peak figure could not be pinned to a single authoritative vintage (the contemporaneous bulletin said 11.6%), so it is dropped rather than shipped uncertain.
